biography: Héctor Rebaque, hailing from the sun-baked streets of Mexico City, always felt the pull of speed. His father, a successful businessman with a penchant for vintage sports cars, instilled a love for motorsport early on. Héctor's racing journey began with go-karts on a makeshift track in his family's warehouse, where he honed his defensive driving style, fiercely protecting his position even against older, more experienced rivals. This scrappy determination caught the eye of a local racing team, leading to a stint in Formula Ford. Now, at 21, Rebaque finds himself at Team Lotus 79, a meteoric rise that has some whispering about nepotism, but Héctor is determined to prove his worth. His debut season has been a rollercoaster, flashes of brilliance overshadowed by rookie mistakes, yet the raw talent is undeniable, waiting to be refined.
drivingStyle: Rebaque is a defensive driver to his core. He's known for his incredible blocking ability and unwavering focus on maintaining track position. He is a master of late braking, often surprising opponents with his ability to squeeze into tight gaps. While not the fastest in outright pace, Rebaque excels in wheel-to-wheel combat, making him a formidable opponent in any race. Tire management is still a work in progress, often pushing too hard in the early stages, leading to struggles in the final laps.

rivalries.reason: A fellow Mexican driver, Vargas represents the established elite, and has openly criticized Rebaque's rapid ascent to Formula 1.
Dubois, known for his aggressive overtaking, has had several on-track clashes with Rebaque, resulting in heated exchanges post-race.
Tanaka is a consistently fast driver who seems to always be right behind Rebaque in races, constantly putting pressure on him. The two have fought many times for position.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of worn-out driving gloves his father gave him.
Listens to mariachi music before every race to calm his nerves.
Has a small, hand-carved wooden jaguar that he keeps in his race car.
famousQuote: Position is everything. Speed will come, but you can't win if you aren't ahead.
careerHighlight: Qualifying 7th at the Monaco Grand Prix, showcasing his raw talent and defensive prowess on the tight street circuit.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the Brazilian Grand Prix on the first lap after a collision with Jean-Pierre Dubois, resulting in a DNF and considerable damage to his car.
